newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan bill governs post-1997 ties with Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan bill governs post-1997 ties with Hong Kong.

text.p: Future ties between Taiwan and the post-1997 Hong Kong will hinge on the passage of a relations bill scheduled to be screened on Friday, officials said Thursday.

"Lawmakers will have a second reading of the Hong Kong and Macao Relation Act during a legislature meeting on Friday," William Li, director of the Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Department under the cabinet-level Mainland Affairs Council, told Reuters.

He said the bill, which prescribes Taiwan's economic and non-political ties with Hong Kong after July 1, 1997, has passed the first reading in December 1996, and there was an urgent need to finalise the bill before the Hong Kong handover.
Hong Kong will be returned to China on July 1, 1997 after 150 years of colonial rule by Britain. The Portuguese colony of Macao will revert to Chinese rule in 1999.
Officials of the Mainland Affairs Council, which formulates China policies, said the bill would provide legal framework for direct links with Hong Kong and Macau.
Under the bill, Hong Kong and Macau will be taken as special administrative zones to skirt the long-standing policy of no direct contact with China.
Taiwan and China have remained political rivals since a civil war split them in 1949, and Taipei maintains a ban on direct links with China.
The bill also seeks to maintain Taiwan's current trade, investment and cultural links with Hong Kong, officials said.
